name: root-structure-policy
purpose: Defines root-level directory classes so the workspace can distinguish registered projects, shared operating folders, local-only folders, and generated outputs.

reader_guide.summary: Open this file when deciding whether a root folder should become a project, a shared operations folder, a private local-only folder, or ignored generated output.
how_to_read: Read directory_classes first to understand the allowed root folder categories.
Use reserved_operational_dirs for tracked shared workspace folders.
Use local_only_dirs for folders that may exist on disk but must not become durable knowledge sources.
Use project_registry_path to find tracked root projects and ownership boundaries.
Run the structure audit command before and after root-level structure changes.
update_triggers: A new root-level folder category is introduced.
A root-level project is created, archived, or renamed.
A local-only or generated-output folder appears at repository root.
Project boundary rules or reserved workspace folders change.
The structure-audit tool reports unknown root folders.

structure_rules.rule: Every tracked non-underscore root directory must be registered in _ops/projects/registry.json unless it is a documented local-only or generated-output directory.
structure_rules.reason: Unregistered root folders make ownership and lifecycle ambiguous.

structure_rules.rule: Reserved operational directories must contain shared workspace assets, not project-specific work that belongs inside a project folder.
structure_rules.reason: Shared folders should reduce repeated work, not hide project ownership.

structure_rules.rule: Local-only directories may exist on disk but must be ignored by git and must not be used as durable source-of-truth for future agents.
structure_rules.reason: Private local scratch state can disappear or contain material that should not be committed or indexed.

structure_rules.rule: Generated build outputs should stay inside the owning project and be ignored unless the artifact is intentionally committed as a durable deliverable.
structure_rules.reason: Root-level generated output folders become hard to attribute and can confuse project boundaries.

structure_rules.rule: Each registered project's durable top-level directories should be listed in that project registry entry's project_specific_home list unless they match generated_output_dirs.
structure_rules.reason: A maintainer should be able to understand project folder purpose from the registry without inspecting every file.

structure_rules.rule: Run the structure audit before and after root-level folder changes, project creation, archive moves, or reserved-folder changes.
structure_rules.reason: A deterministic check catches ambiguous folders before they become long-lived conventions.

field_guide.meaning: Path to the source-of-truth registry for tracked root projects.
Allowed conceptual categories for root-level directories.
Tracked underscore-prefixed folders for shared workspace operations and knowledge.
Root folders that may exist locally but must stay ignored and non-authoritative.
Known generated or dependency directories that should stay project-local and ignored.
Deterministic command for checking root structure against this policy.

directory_classes.description: Root project with its own purpose, lifecycle, README, commands, and project registry entry.
Tracked underscore-prefixed shared workspace folder for cross-project rules, operations, templates, tools, research, or history.
Ignored private or scratch folder that can exist locally but is not durable repository state.
Ignored build output, dependency cache, or generated runtime state owned by a project.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _docs
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Workspace-level documentation, policies, and decision records.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _history
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Dated work history, request summaries, traces, evaluations, plans, installations, and context archives.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _ops
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Operations hub, prompts, workflows, coordination, maps, project registry, and install registry.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _philosophy
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Foundational agent and platform operating philosophy.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _requirements
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Shared requirements baselines, changes, and reviews.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _research
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Reusable internet research and external reference notes.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _skills
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Tracked source copies of custom Codex skills.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _specs
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Shared spec-driven artifacts, plans, tasks, validation, and traceability.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _templates
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Reusable project, document, research, and artifact templates.

reserved_operational_dirs.name: _tools
reserved_operational_dirs.purpose: Reusable deterministic local tools and scripts.

local_only_dirs.name: _private
local_only_dirs.purpose: Local private notes or scratch state that must not be committed or used as durable knowledge.

local_only_dirs.name: outputs
local_only_dirs.purpose: Transient local output from one-off tool runs; durable artifacts must move into the owning project artifacts folder.

generated_output_dirs.purpose: Next.js build cache and runtime output.
Project-local distributable build output that can be regenerated.
Project-local compiled build output that can be regenerated.
Static export output that can be regenerated from project source.
